items.t: In King George Corridor, houses sold at a median of $1,345,000 across 71 sales, and the middle half closed between $1,179,950 and $1,515,000. The median house sat 21 days and sold for 96.7% of list.
King George Corridor: 77 townhomes sold at a median of $776,000, with the middle half between $730,000 and $888,000. The median townhome took 25 days to sell and closed at 96.9% of list.

123 condos sold in King George Corridor at a median of $553,000 (middle half $497,500 to $610,250). A typical condo in King George Corridor spent 29 days on the market and closed at 97.1% of the asking price.

blocks.text: Source: Paragon closed sales, November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026; medians need 5 or more sales.
How King George Corridor compares with the rest of South Surrey and White Rock

items.t: Houses in King George Corridor have the lowest median of the 8 South Surrey and White Rock sub-areas, $1,345,000, below Sunnyside Park Surrey at $1,434,500; the highest is Elgin Chantrell at $2,280,000.
Townhomes in King George Corridor have the lowest median of the 8 South Surrey and White Rock sub-areas, $776,000, below Morgan Creek at $785,000; the highest is Elgin Chantrell at $1,242,500.

Of 7 South Surrey and White Rock sub-areas with 5 or more condo sales, King George Corridor ranks 4th highest at $553,000; the range is $506,500 (Sunnyside Park Surrey) to $1,035,000 (Crescent Beach and Ocean Park). Morgan Creek ($552,500) sits just below and Grandview ($565,000) sits just above.

blocks.text: By build year, townhomes are the newest homes selling in King George Corridor (median 2008) and houses the oldest (median 1988), a gap of 20 years.
